answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity bond. Each account escrows a fixed stake on-chain, and every identity posts its own full amount, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand deposits. That umber of accounts raises the attacker's floor price linearly while influence per extra voice stays flat. Funding sources are linked, so a cluster sharing one wallet counts as a single vote. A bond is slashed into an insurer pool when its identity fails review, and the node leaves the horizon of accepted participants that epoch. A harbor full of Sybil accounts keeps paying upkeep, so cost wins.
